I have issue with this game's original story content, but the extra prequel story does make it up for. The game was super difficult at beginning, but trivialized once you mastered all mechanics.

Spirit of Amazonia truly make up for its original linear game, and make you rethink all knowledge that you had previously. Now with end of SoA part 3, the game truly shine in its sandbox + story gameplay.

Ability to coop with friends made it much more fun.
Also, I cant wait to try the VR version soon.

Pro-Tip: The first thing you should make is a bow and arrow. Bow = 1x long stick and 1x rope. Arrows = x2 bird feathers and x1 stick each. Look for dead birds on then ground and harvest them for feathers. Once you have that the combat is trivial. This game has a "hold breath" mechanic with Left-Shift for keyboard. You can basically beat all combat with the tried and true method of "shoot them in the face."

I played this back in 2020 with friends and we kinda got tired of it quick. I've revisited this in August 2023 because I never played the single player story. People tend to spurn this game because its steep starting learning curve because it does not hold your hand. Gotta google that shit or trial-and-error to figure it out. I found out most things via the latter because I hate myself. But once you figure it out, combat and survival is trivial, the only challenge is knowing where the fuck you are on the map.

I will say though, the story turned out to be something I completely didn't expect, and was actually quite pleased with it. Once you finish it, you'll soon realize why the game is aptly named "Green Hell."

Great Game I Currently have 76 Hours in it, It's hard at First and you have to Experiment just like you'd try to Survive IRL you will Die a Ton Early on until you get use to it the Only Issue I have is no Support for Dedicated Servers I own my Servers and would love to Host a Game so My Friends and I can Play at Different Times on the Same Game since our Schedules don't always Match, So if you like Multiplayer but Can't be on at the Same time as the Host then this isn't the Game for you but if you like a Great Single Player Experience and can be on when your Friends are on this will get you there

This is 10/10 game! Perfect graphics and scenery. From the ground to the sky the game is perfect. I would recommend this to people that love survival and openworld games. And remember the jungle is not forgiving...

After 20+hrs of offline gameplay, I'm moving on from the game.
I give it a 7/10.

First time I played I savoured the great graphics and scenery that lies before me, but what awestruck me is how you can interact with everything that I thought was just a model for background. I mean like any amazon jungle it's filled with plants and trees and to think all  these resources were spawned to make a naturally nice scenery.

For the game, you will encounter lots of events/accidents that when not dealt properly will lower your health/sanity which will lead to death. Knowing the proper treatment and having a base to settle down is pretty much end content and easy to acquire. You have to roam the jungle though to find recipes to craft new tools like more traps, beds, etc but risk of encountering danger from tigers to leeches.

Some people compare it to Rust, but this is PVE oriented, and the base you build can't be as complex as Rust. And it doesn't support multiplayer as of now nor the weapons inclined for a PVP.

As it's still in the early access, it has a lots of bugs during loads. And the story isn't done yet, although the tutorial/early story was well made and recommended to knowing the game. Overall give this game a chance.
This is a 10/10 for me just by playing it for 4 hours straight, using the free weekend, this makes me wanna buy the game now, Again you deserve my Praise.
This game is very immersive, difficult, and gross at times. A must-play for any hardcore survival game fans.

So much fun with and without friends. This game is challenging and intriguing. Playing without a window open in the background for instructions is almost impossible and I tried to do it without. It made the game take so much longer to progress which was tedious but extremely rewarding. The curiosity of being alone in the jungle and stumbling upon empty camps and structures was while trying to avoid certain death was stressful yet exhilarating. I like to describe the game as a first person modernization jungle themed version of the Oregon Trail game. 7.5/10

Great game if you like survival games, which I do. Go at your own pace. Explore, craft, build, discover, follow the story line, make it as hard as you want it to be. Move at your own pace and difficulty. There's a lot to do and it doesn't get boring.

I love survival games, but this game does not want you to survive, The Jungle hates you, and in my first 30 minutes I had died twice at my starting location. I had worms, parasites, leeches and all kinds of things hanging off me, letting me know that I am not welcome here. The learning curve is steep, you are going to die a lot just by tripping over a log into a bush and coming out with all kinds of nasty things attached to you. The first 10 days will really put you to the test, are you cut out for survival or in fact this game. But you ca learn, then restart your game and give yourself a better starting chance to survive. After those 10 days where you WILL come close to dying multiple times, you start to get to a point where you are no longer surviving, you are living and thriving. This is where the game really takes off and becomes addictive, you wont want to turn it off and you will want to explore, but beware, there is no real effective map system to help you, jsut your watch co ordinates and you WILL get turned around very easily and maybe never find your way back to your base. The game looks beautiful, the crafting and menu system is a bit awkward at first but you do get used to it, and you will love shitting out parasites and worms. Love it.

I loved this game for the first 2 or 3 days playing it. However, after figuring out the game mechanics and getting a home base set up the game becomes extremely boring. Water is very easy to collect with coconuts and fish is very plentiful and easy to catch. The big gerbil looking thing are very easy to kill for meat. I have crafted everything available. Items like the bamboo smoker and grill make loading up on food easy. I have explored all over and after you go to the known "loot" spots there is anything left to see really. The available loot like chips, juice, peanuts, and a rusty machete is pretty much all there is...like literally.... that’s it.

The game is fantastic but after mastering the survival part and exploring for about a day....it leaves you without much to do and in the constant cycle of cook, eat, rain, drink, sleep, remove leech. A great start for an early access but anxious for more.

The success of this game greatly depends on how much it gets developed. The small preview of the story is fantastic, and I know that will make things interesting. I just hope the game comes to full release soon instead of later or never like a lot of early release games.

I am not going to be reviewing gameplay, I will be reviewing technical side of the game.
Runs very poorly at 1080 gtx, ryzen 3600, 32gb ram, tried all fixes, nothing helped.
You cannot disable Depth of Field
You cannot disable Motion Blur
You cannot disable fisheye lens effect the game has. The camera is always distorted around the edges and from googling, it makes a lot of people nauseous including me. I am addicted to games and played pretty much any worth mentioning game there is and never got nauseous before.

The multiplayer experience is ultimately so buggy and unpolished that a 15 hour save and the entire folder housing it can disappear. This was on top of hours of backtracking because respawn points worked sporadically at best.

My biggest regret is that these issues didn't come up within the 2-hour refund period so I can at least get my money back. Creepy Jar should be embarrassed to release a product with this kind of technical issue.

It's a really fun game in my opinion. It can get difficult at parts but what I love most is on top of the good survival mechanics, you can go at your own pace, explore and be creative. I hope that this game will keep on having new content added, although there's already a lot of stuff to do, so it doesn't get boring. I also really like the way that damage & health is dealt with in this game, it forces you to pay attention to the little things without being too cryptic.

Green Hell delivers an intense and immersive survival experience, combining a gripping story with deep survival mechanics. Navigating the harsh Amazon rainforest while managing food, hydration, and sanity creates an engaging challenge—at least for a while. Early on, hunting, foraging, and balancing nutrients is rewarding, but once a farm is set up, the survival aspect starts feeling more like a grind.

Where the game truly shines is in co-op. Playing with friends makes survival feel more dynamic and enjoyable, as teamwork adds an extra layer of strategy and fun. The jungle feels even more alive when you’re not facing it alone. While the survival mechanics can become repetitive, the overall experience—especially in multiplayer—makes Green Hell a great choice for fans of hardcore survival games.

If you're into painfully realistic, difficult survival crafting games, you'll love this one. Everything is dangerous and the game doesn't tell you much at all about how to survive. Beautiful scenery filled with things that all want to kill you. The co-op is great, didn't have any issues staying connected or with lag.

Highlights:
Cool ayahuasca trip through the jungle.
(some) Cute wildlife that doesn't want to eat you.
Fighting the jungle cats is pretty fun once you get used to it and have a bow.
Amazing view literally every step you take.
Intuitive building.
Medicine, food, etc. all heavily realistic and easy to figure out if you have some survival knowledge going in.

Not so highlights:
Early game, you will die. A lot.
Very realistic spiders.
You can't skin the jungle cats for their fur, which would be cool.
A mistake as small as crossing a river without looking will often lead to a spiral that takes days to recover from, especially if you don't already have a camp set up.

Went in water, got stung by bees, scorpion and snakes.
Died a bejillion times... made a hut, went psychotic and started hearing voices and seeing people who werent really there. Only to die from people who werent really there killing me!

If you liked the forest but wanted more resource and crafting mechanics, this game may interest you. The small chunk of story that we're able to see seems interesting and the survival mode is pretty fun. The game needs more things to do, but it seems the devs have been hitting their roadmap goals so i'm not worried about that aspect of the game. My only current complaints are that the game does not seem to have enough methods to heal yourself when injured in comparison to the plethora of injuries you can get from various sources. The other complaint is that the game seems poorly optimized, but this is early access so who's to say better optimization isn't coming with the next update or two.
Overall I would recommend this game in it's current state for $20. It has enough content to entertain me indefinitely and seeing how the devs are actively working on the game, I imagine it's only going to get better by the end of the year.

Saving is impossible (at least for me) in story mode. I built the shelter and slept in it, but the game was not saved. At the end of numerous trial, I gave up..
And the difficulty... I convinced myself that I can finish dark souls without taking any damage rather than playing this game.

THE best crafting survival game I've ever played, the jungle is not a friendly place and Green Hell nails it's survival elements. Be ready to learn the hard way a LOT. I suggest you get a notepad and start writing down useful things you've learned like what each item does for you, example, charcoal removes food poisoning and tobacco is an anti-venom.

10/10 thoroughly recommend this game. Survival mode is my favorite.

As a lover of survival games and realism, this game tries to combine both and nearly succeeds. However I feel a lot of the game is difficult just for the sake of being difficult. I've spent countless hours on sandbox survival games as well as story driven. This is by far one of the most realistic versions I have played. However, the inventory is clunky, tasks are monotonous and the game is by far the most unforgiving. If you're looking for a realistic survival simulator, then by all means buy this game. However I have a hard time recommending this for someone like me, who's looking for a seemingly realistic survival game with just enough difficulty to still be fun and challenging.

Edit: **Purchased Again**

After updates and additions to the game, I can safely recommend this game to any survival game enthusiast, plenty to do, steep learning curve but satisfying. Get the basics down, beat the story, then try the SoA mode.

I don't know if I'm more intimidated by the ground worms that crawl under your skin or the relentless visual reminder that the enemies have GINORMOUS ... gourds ...regardless, it's a 10/10. I got attacked from behind by a puma on my first day and didn't know what it was and I thought it was a grizzly bear because I'm dumb and my tiny, terrified brain didn't even stop to think of why a godd*mn GRIZZLY BEAR would be in the jungle.

This game is really good, it is solid all the way around and is still being developed, so it will still likely improve. I would recommend to anyone even slightly interested in this one. Green Hell Yeah.
